blocks.text: Destination IP groups are used as a single, reusable object to enforce rules across various security policies. You can apply destination IP groups to policies, such as Firewall Filtering, NAT Control, DNS Control, IPS Control, and Forwarding Control.
Destination IP groups provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Combine destination IP addresses and FQDNs, destination countries, and URL categories into groups so you can manage them collectively in security policies.
Use destination IP groups as rule criteria in various policy rules to control your outbound traffic and enforce condition-based actions on your network traffic.
Automate policy updates by modifying IP addresses or URL categories within a group once to automatically apply those changes across all linked security controls, minimizing configuration errors.

blocks.text: Destination IPv4 and IPv6 addresses are managed in separate groups. The Zscaler service provides two predefined groups (All IPv4 and All IPv6) that contain all addresses of their respective types. Additionally, you can create custom groups for IPv4 addresses using individual IP addresses, subnets, or ranges to define specific network segments.

blocks.item: Custom groups based on IPv6 addresses are not currently supported.
In SSL/TLS Inspection and DNS Control policies, IP-based destination groups used in rule criteria are ignored during policy evaluation if an SNI value is present in HTTPS requests.

blocks.text: You can use the following pages to create and manage destination IP address groups:

blocks.item: About the Destination IPv4 Groups Page
On the Destination IPv4 Groups page (Internet Access > Resources > IP & FQDN Groups > Destination IPv4 Groups), you can do the following:
Search for a destination IPv4 group.
Add a destination IPv4 group.
Modify the table and its columns.
View the list of all destination IPv4 groups. For each IPv4 group, you can view:
Name: The name of the destination group. You can sort this column.
Type: The type of the destination group, such as IP Address, FQDN, Wildcard FQDN, or Other.
IP Address, FQDN or WildCard FQDN: The IP addresses, FQDNs, or wildcard FQDNs included in the group.
Countries: The countries included in the group.
Description: The description of the group, if available. You can sort this column.
Categories: The custom URL categories included in the group.
Edit or delete a destination IPv4 group.
View information about the predefined All IPv4 group.
The destination IPv4 groups are paginated with up to 500 groups displayed per page.
Go to the Source IPv4 Groups, Source IPv6 Groups, Destination IPv6 Groups, and IP Pool pages.
About the Destination IPv6 Groups Page
On the Destination IPv6 Groups page (Internet Access > Resources > IP & FQDN Groups > Destination IPv6 Groups), you can do the following:
Search for a destination IPv6 group.
Modify the table and its columns.
View the available destination IPv6 groups. Currently, only the predefined All IPv6 group is available. For this group, you can view:
Name: The name of the destination group. You can sort this column.
Type: The type of the destination group, such as IP Address, FQDN, Wildcard FQDN, or Other.
IP Address, FQDN or WildCard FQDN: The IP addresses, FQDNs, and wildcard FQDNs included in the group.
Countries: The countries included in the group.
Description: The description of the group, if available.
Categories: The custom URL categories included in the group.
Actions: An option to view details about this group.
View details for read-only predefined groups.
Pagination is supported to display up to 500 groups per page.
Go to the Source IPv4 Groups, Source IPv6 Groups, Destination IPv4 Groups, and IP Pool pages.
